analysis:
The only change in this batch is documentation in docs/reference/configuration.md. It adds a "Prompt preparation and admission" section at head lines 587-596, after the model-verification I/O section. The patch excerpt is truncated at the last table row (`DARKBLOOM_TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE`). Unit :5 (head text) covers only head lines 1-353, so the new rows are visible only through the patch excerpt and I could not cite them at a head line. Unit :4 (base lines 520-687) is unchanged context. No source code, enforcement logic or defaults changed in the supplied evidence, so I found no concrete regression and raised no findings.

The new rows describe a prompt-token cache (`PromptTokenCache.swift`, `PromptTokenCachePolicy`) with these properties:
- It reuses token IDs of rendered chat-template pieces "already seen in the request's prefix-cache scope".
- It is on by default, with a 32 MiB LRU per tokenizer.
- It is disabled by the global `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0`.
- It is forwarded by the LaunchAgent.
- A background verifier re-tokenizes prompts and disables reuse on mismatch.
- Template-loop rewrites are on by default.

This is a new in-process store keyed by prompt content, so it relates to A-001 and to T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and TTFT timing oracle, with SEC-035 as the accepted same-account risk) and T-028 (residual data). Whether it holds up depends on code not supplied:
- Is the cache keyed strictly by the coordinator-authored cacheSalt/account scope, so reuse cannot cross accounts?
- Is it memory-only, with no on-disk artifacts? The doc is silent on this; no persistence is stated.
- Does the piece-level hit/miss timing difference stay within the accepted same-account oracle?
- Is the background verifier's re-tokenization safe against the same inputs, and does the "first 4 prompts" verification fail closed?

The doc says the cache is scope-limited, but I cannot verify that from the supplied evidence. The next pass should check that T-041 is updated to mention the prompt-token cache and its scope key if the code shows it is not covered. Existing unchanged text in unit :4 (SSD prefix cache settings) is pre-existing and not restated.
